Sara D (People Ops): Heads up — launching a short pilot for On‑call Recovery Days starting Apr 1. Goal: give folks time to reset after high‑impact on‑call incidents. Details below and a link to the lightweight request form. :sparkles:

Alex M (Eng): Nice — what counts as a high‑impact incident?

Sara D (People Ops): Good q. For the pilot, eligible incidents are: >3 hours of continuous active paging or paging spanning a production incident that required a postmortem (P0/P1). We’ll keep this intentionally broad to start.

Priya S (SRE): Will this be auto‑approved or need direct manager signoff?

Sara D (People Ops): Managers will receive a notification but the request will be auto‑approved if it meets the criteria. We want to reduce friction. Managers can flag exceptions.

Jamal K (Director): Is there a cap? We don’t want people taking recovery days for every small blip.

Sara D (People Ops): Yep — pilot rules: max 2 On‑call Recovery Days per quarter per person, must be taken within 14 days of the incident, and they’re additive to your existing PTO (not a replacement). If an incident spans multiple people, each eligible on‑call responder can request a recovery day.

Priya S (SRE): How do we log this in the HR system?

Sara D (People Ops): Use time off type "On‑call Recovery" in the HR portal. We’ve added a quick form at https://redwood.internal/hr/oncall‑recovery to prefill the request (please paste pager/incident link). hr‑bot will post a confirmation once it’s recorded.

Alex M (Eng): And travel / workation conflicts? If someone is mid‑travel, can they still use the day?

Sara D (People Ops): Should coordinate with your manager. The automatic approval still applies but managers can convert it to an equivalent remote rest day if needed.

Priya S (SRE): Anything special for Dedicated/private infra teams who have different oncall rotations?

Sara D (People Ops): Applies to all teams with documented oncall rotations (hosted/dedicated/private). If your team uses different postmortem thresholds, ping me and we can add a team‑specific rule in the pilot.

Jamal K (Director): How long is the pilot?

Sara D (People Ops): 3 months. We’ll evaluate uptake, manager feedback, and any gaming patterns. Expect a short survey after the pilot and we’ll share metrics (days taken, team distribution, common incident tags).

Alex M (Eng): Love it. Can we get a short blurb for team channels so managers can share?

Sara D (People Ops): On it — I’ll post a one‑pager + suggested Slack blurb later today. For now: TL;DR — new On‑call Recovery Day pilot, Apr 1, 2 days/quarter, request via HR form, auto‑approved if incident meets criteria. :white_check_mark:

Priya S (SRE): Thanks — very timely. This will help reduce burnout after big incidents. :heart:

hr‑bot: Confirmation: On‑call Recovery time off type has been added to the HR portal. Refer to https://redwood.internal/hr/oncall‑recovery for the form and policy doc.
